checks: Complete the square in L_j(z) to get radius at least 3ε/4 on the full real base interval. At k the roof gap is greater than ε/2 for every j≠k, so the winning roof is stable on a relative neighborhood and every integer fiber is the stated positive homothet.

At each group an interior real base near its sampled k retains strict slack for all other roofs. A relative interior point of each irredundant scaled K facet sweeps an ambient facet patch, so every listed ambient group normal is genuine. Both endpoint base faces are full-dimensional fibers and hence facets.

The sampled volume is a sum of independent V r_k^d terms. Each r_k is positive and d≥2, giving N+1 positive Hessian directions. The result concerns tied offsets within each roof group, an open parameter cube of the specified dimension.

Twice differentiating r^d F((b−ak)/r) gives the stated three terms and signs. The centered simplex vertex cap through its centroid scales with the fiber, so its raw mass is exactly γ_d M(h) and the normalized ratio is constant.
Read d0bf1dbafd292ae0 §§1–3, (1)–(5). The draft claims no depth stationarity and uses the actual ambient fixed-facet-normal polytope, strengthening the explicit check of facet irredundancy.

overlap.comparison: Its index bound is for a least-active stochastic maximizer of a row objective. These offset coordinates and sampled mixed-volume Hessian do not satisfy that model.
Its cap Hessian is angular on a single convex body; this construction fixes cap and ambient body normals while varying the sampled fiber radii.

readability: The ambient facet normals are fixed while the offset parameter is tied across each roof group's facets. The raw Hessian is computed in this exact specified chart.
review_method: Independent proof read of the exact frozen candidate and check of its sources and predecessors. Exact rational replay for the distal and two-triangle numerical certificates.
summary: Actual irredundant ambient facets and complete positive fibers realize an arbitrarily large positive Hessian index in the tied offset chart, also for a raw cap of constant normalized fraction.
